//: The truth harness's own TypeScript check (DI-49). Not a build: `noEmit`, and the only
thing it decides is whether the printed modules and the adapter they call are well typed
under the pinned compiler (`ts/eff/node_modules/.bin/tsc`, 5.9.2). Evidence word: tested —
a finite checker run, never byte reproduction (DI-32).
Two callers, one file. `scripts/check-truth.py` copies this config beside the freshly
regenerated `prelude.ts` and `generated/` in its work directory and runs `tsc --noEmit -p`
there before it compares any byte, so the check is on the modules rc.112 just ran, not on
the committed copies; running `tsc --noEmit -p harness/truth/tsconfig.json` from the
repository root checks the committed tree the same way.
What is in scope: the printed images (`generated/*.ts`) and the adapter they call
(`prelude.ts`). What is not: `run-truth.ts`, the recorder, which is not a printed image and
has three diagnostics under these options that predate this gate — `option`'s
`argv[index + 1]` and `failPayloads`' element type under `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, and
`TracedScheduler.makeDispatcher`, whose base returns rc.112's unexported
`MixedSchedulerDispatcher` (`vendor/effect-4.0.0-rc.112/src/Scheduler.ts:188-193`) so the
override's narrower `SchedulerDispatcher` cannot be named. Widening this gate to the
recorder means expressing `TracedScheduler` as a delegating `Scheduler.Scheduler`; that is
its own change, with the schedule rows of `result.json` as its evidence.
The options are `ts/eff/tsconfig.json`'s, verbatim: one compiler, one dialect, two gates.
`effect` and `@types/bun` resolve through `harness/truth/node_modules`, the link
`check-truth.py` makes to the pinned installation.
